## Pull request overview

Implements namespace-aware component registration to avoid type collisions across packages/plugins, and introduces (intended) lazy field registration to reduce field-related bundle cost.

**Changes:**
- Added `namespace` support to `ComponentRegistry` registration/lookup and updated many component registrations to use it.
- Added lazy field registration APIs (`registerField`, `registerAllFields`) and a field widget loader map.
- Updated build/tooling configs (Turbo v2 config key, pnpm config, CI workflows) and added migration docs.

The backward-compat alias entry (non-namespaced key) is only created when it doesn’t already exist. If a namespaced component is later re-registered (overwriting the namespaced key), the alias key will still point to the old component, so `get('table')` can return a different renderer than `get('table', 'ui')`. Consider always updating the alias entry when writing a namespaced registration, or store aliases separately so overwrites keep aliases consistent.

This dynamic index into `LucideIcons` will fail TypeScript under `noImplicitAny`/`noUncheckedIndexedAccess` because `typeof LucideIcons` has no string index signature (this was previously suppressed by `@ts-expect-error`). Reintroduce a safe cast (e.g., cast `LucideIcons` to `Record<string, LucideIcon>`), or implement a type guard so the file still type-checks.

CI no longer pins the pnpm version. If `pnpm/action-setup@v4` doesn’t reliably honor the repo’s `packageManager: pnpm@9.0.0`, this can cause non-reproducible installs (especially across pnpm major versions). Consider explicitly setting the pnpm version from `packageManager`, or enable Corepack and rely on it consistently.

Namespace support changes component resolution semantics (aliasing, overwrite behavior, and `get(type, namespace)` priority). There are existing Vitest tests in this package (`packages/core/src/registry/__tests__`), but none covering the Registry. Add tests for: (1) registering with a namespace creates the expected namespaced key, (2) non-namespaced fallback behavior, and (3) overwrite behavior doesn’t leave stale aliases.

`registerField()` creates a `React.lazy(...)` widget and passes it into `createFieldRenderer(...)`, but the current field renderer does not wrap the widget with `React.Suspense`. Rendering a lazy widget without a Suspense boundary will throw at runtime. Consider wrapping the lazy widget in a Suspense fallback inside `registerField()` (or adjusting `createFieldRenderer` accordingly) so lazy field loading actually works.

`getAllConfigs()` / `getNamespaceComponents()` return values from the internal map, which includes both the namespaced key and the backward-compat alias key for the same component. This can double-count components in UIs that list configs by namespace. Consider de-duping by the map key (e.g., only include keys that start with `${namespace}:`) or add an `isAlias` flag and filter aliases out.

The JSDoc says `registerAllFields()` “auto-registers all field widgets on import”, but this module no longer calls `registerAllFields()`/`registerFields()` at top level. This breaks the documented/backward-compatible pattern `import '@object-ui/fields'` (e.g., Storybook uses it). Either restore a side-effect entrypoint that auto-registers all fields (recommended: separate export like `@object-ui/fields/register-all`) or update docs and all call sites accordingly.

New public APIs `registerField()` / `registerAllFields()` introduce important behavior (lazy loading, unknown-field handling, and registry registration under the `field` namespace). The fields package already has Vitest tests; please add tests that verify these functions register the expected component types (e.g. `field:text`) and that rendering works (including Suspense fallback for lazy widgets).
